summary: Enfortumab Vedotin (Padcev) is a Nectin-4-directed antibody-drug conjugate indicated for Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer after prior platinum and PD-1/PD-L1 therapy (and in combination with pembrolizumab as first-line per labeling). Signature toxicities are severe skin reactions including SJS/TEN (boxed; hold for grade 3+, discontinue for confirmed SJS/TEN), hyperglycaemia (including DKA), peripheral neuropathy, ocular disorders and extravasation injury.
indications: Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer after prior platinum and PD-1/PD-L1 therapy (and in combination with pembrolizumab as first-line per labeling)

dosage.d: 1.25 mg/kg (maximum 125 mg) on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle
dosage.t: IV infusion per labeling; do not substitute for other ADCs or naked antibodies
dosage.n: Dose-hold/reduce for neutropenia, neuropathy, ocular or skin toxicity per grade

admin: For IV infusion after dilution; do not give IV push or bolus
Verify the exact ADC label before every dose (multiple ADCs share infusion settings but not doses)
Premedicate and use supportive care per payload class (antiemetics, eye care, neuropathy review)
moa: Antibody binds the tumour-surface target; receptor-mediated endocytosis followed by linker cleavage releases the cytotoxic payload intracellularly, killing the target cell with limited systemic exposure relative to free chemotherapy.

relative: Severe pre-existing payload-class toxicity (e.g. severe neuropathy, ocular disease) - individualise

preg: No adequate human data. Based on mechanism, fetal harm is expected. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose. Use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Because of potential serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose.
renal: No formal dose adjustment; monitor renal function with nephrotoxic payloads or dehydration from GI effects.
hepatic: No formal dose adjustment; payloads are hepatically cleared - monitor LFTs and bilirubin closely in impairment.

major: Strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors or inducers (may alter payload exposure; monitor toxicity/efficacy)
Other myelosuppressive or neurotoxic agents (additive risk)
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; counsel on concomitant risks.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

rare: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (reported with some ADC/antibody classes)
emergency: Fever with neutropenia - seek urgent care
Severe skin blistering/peeling - seek emergency care
Sudden vision change or eye pain - seek urgent eye evaluation

monitoring: Payload-class toxicity review (neuropathy, eyes, skin, lungs)
counsel: Report numbness, tingling or burning in hands/feet (nerve effects)
Report eye dryness, pain, redness or vision change promptly (eye effects with several ADCs)
Report rash, blistering or skin peeling at once
Fever during treatment needs urgent evaluation (low blood counts)
Use effective contraception; do not breastfeed
pk: End of infusion (conjugate); payload acts intracellularly
Days (IgG-based conjugate); every-3-week or weekly schedules
Continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity
Refrigerate 2-8 C; do not freeze; use diluted solution promptly per labeling
pearls: ADCs are not interchangeable - same antibody with a different payload is a different drug with different dosing and toxicity
Blood glucose monitoring is routine even in non-diabetics (hyperglycaemia/DKA risk)
Skin toxicity can be fatal - early dermatology input and strict hold rules
missed: If a planned dose is missed, give it as soon as possible and adjust the schedule to maintain the planned interval; do not double the dose. Consult the full prescribing information for cycle-delay rules.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose is expected to exaggerate known toxicities (myelosuppression, GI effects, infusion reactions). Provide supportive care with close monitoring. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
